title: npx, Yarn PnP, and Execution Models
description: Explore package execution with npx, yarn dlx, and Plug and Play.

data.text: Running package binaries and managing execution environments are crucial for developer productivity and security.
npx executes binaries from node_modules/.bin or fetches packages temporarily without installing them.

data.caption: Run create-react-app without installing globally
data.code:
npx create-react-app my-app
npx eslint src/**/*.ts

data.text: yarn dlx is Yarn's equivalent to npx. It downloads the package to a global cache and runs it.

data.caption: Run a package with Yarn Dlx

data.text: PnP eliminates node_modules entirely. Instead, Yarn stores packages in a global cache and generates a .pnp.cjs loader file.

data.title: Compatibility
data.text: Some tools do not support PnP out of the box. Check compatibility before migrating a project.

data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[Source Code] --> B[.pnp.cjs]
    B --> C[Global Cache]
    C --> D[Package Binary]
    D --> E[Execution]
    F[node_modules] -.->|Not used| E
data.caption: PnP execution flow vs node_modules

items.question: Is PnP faster?
items.answer: Yes. It avoids disk I/O from node_modules and improves install speed significantly.

items.question: Can I mix PnP and node_modules?
items.answer: No. A project must choose one strategy.

items.text: npx and yarn dlx run binaries without global installs.
PnP removes node_modules for faster installs.
Verify tool compatibility before adopting PnP.
